items.question: A central bank targets inflation of 4 percent, with a tolerance band from 2 percent to 6 percent. Inflation is 4 percent. Consider the following statements. (1) Inflation is exactly on target. (2) Inflation is within the tolerance band. (3) Inflation has breached the tolerance band. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
items.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: 4 equals the target of 4. Statement 2 is correct: 4 is between 2 and 6. Statement 3 is incorrect: 4 is inside the band, so it has not breached it.

items.question: A country's remittances were Rs 80 crore in 2021, Rs 88 crore in 2022, Rs 96.8 crore in 2023 and Rs 106.48 crore in 2024. Consider the following statements. (1) Remittances grew by 10 percent every year. (2) Total growth from 2021 to 2024 was 33.1 percent. (3) The 2024 value exceeds Rs 106 crore. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
items.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: 80 to 88, 88 to 96.8 and 96.8 to 106.48 are each rises of 10 percent. Statement 2 is correct: 106.48 minus 80 is 26.48, and 26.48 out of 80 is 33.1 percent. Statement 3 is correct: 106.48 is more than 106.

items.question: Four telecom firms have subscribers of 35 crore, 30 crore, 20 crore and 15 crore. Consider the following statements. (1) The firm with 35 crore subscribers has 35 percent of the total. (2) The firms with 30 crore and 20 crore subscribers together have half of the total. (3) The firm with 15 crore subscribers has more than half of the second firm's subscribers. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
items.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: the total is 100 crore, and 35 out of 100 is 35 percent. Statement 2 is correct: 30 plus 20 is 50, which is half of 100. Statement 3 is incorrect: half of 30 is 15, and 15 is not more than 15.

items.question: The 14th Finance Commission was constituted in 2013. The Goods and Services Tax Council was set up in 2016. The 15th Finance Commission was constituted in 2017. Consider the following statements. (1) The 14th Finance Commission came before the Goods and Services Tax Council. (2) The 15th Finance Commission came after the Goods and Services Tax Council. (3) The gap between the 14th and 15th Finance Commissions is 4 years. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
items.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: 2013 comes before 2016. Statement 2 is correct: 2017 comes after 2016. Statement 3 is correct: 2017 minus 2013 is 4.

items.question: A parliamentary committee has 15 members: 9 from the ruling party and 6 from the opposition. Consider the following statements. (1) The ruling party has 60 percent of the seats on the committee. (2) The opposition has more than one-third of the seats. (3) The ruling party has twice as many seats as the opposition. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
items.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: 9 out of 15 is 60 percent. Statement 2 is correct: 6 out of 15 is 40 percent, which is more than one-third. Statement 3 is incorrect: twice 6 is 12, not 9.

items.question: A bank's income is Rs 800 crore: interest income Rs 560 crore, fee income Rs 160 crore and other income Rs 80 crore. Consider the following statements. (1) Interest income accounts for 70 percent of the income. (2) Fee income accounts for one-fifth of the income. (3) Other income is more than fee income. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
items.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: 560 out of 800 is 70 percent. Statement 2 is correct: 160 out of 800 is one-fifth. Statement 3 is incorrect: 80 is less than 160.

items.question: A bank raises its fixed deposit rate from 6.5 percent to 7.0 percent. A depositor has a deposit of Rs 3 lakh. Consider the following statements. (1) The annual interest on the deposit rises from Rs 19,500 to Rs 21,000. (2) The annual interest rises by Rs 1,500. (3) The rise in interest is more than 10 percent of the old interest. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
items.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: 6.5 percent of 3 lakh is 19,500 and 7 percent of 3 lakh is 21,000. Statement 2 is correct: 21,000 minus 19,500 is 1,500. Statement 3 is incorrect: 1,500 out of 19,500 is about 7.7 percent, which is less than 10 percent.

items.question: Country X has gross domestic product of Rs 400 crore and a population of 20 lakh. Country Y has gross domestic product of Rs 900 crore and a population of 60 lakh. Consider the following statements. (1) Country Y's gross domestic product is larger than country X's. (2) Country X's per capita gross domestic product is higher than country Y's. (3) Country Y's per capita gross domestic product is higher than country X's. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
items.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: 900 is larger than 400. Statement 2 is correct: X's per capita figure is 400 divided by 20, or 20, while Y's is 900 divided by 60, or 15. Statement 3 is incorrect: it reverses the comparison.

items.question: A foreign institutional investor holds Rs 200 crore of Indian shares. It sells all Rs 200 crore of shares and buys Rs 200 crore of Indian government bonds. Consider the following statements. (1) The investor's total investment in India is unchanged. (2) The investor has withdrawn from India. (3) The investor still holds Rs 200 crore in Indian securities. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
items.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: 200 sold and 200 bought leaves the total at 200. Statement 2 is incorrect: the money stayed in India, only the form changed from shares to bonds. Statement 3 is correct: the bonds are Indian securities worth Rs 200 crore.

items.question: A bank's profits fell by 10 percent this quarter. Three explanations are offered: higher provisions for bad loans this quarter, a one-time tax charge last quarter, and lower interest income this quarter. Further facts: provisions rose sharply this quarter, the tax charge was last quarter, and interest income was flat this quarter. Consider the following statements. (1) The one-time tax charge is ruled out by timing, because it was last quarter. (2) Lower interest income is ruled out, because interest income was flat. (3) Higher provisions are supported as a cause, because they rose sharply in the same quarter as the fall. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
items.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: a charge last quarter cannot explain a fall this quarter. Statement 2 is correct: flat interest income cannot explain a fall in profits. Statement 3 is correct: provisions rose sharply in the same quarter, which matches the fall in timing and in size.

items.question: A fund must keep at least 80 percent of its money in government securities. It holds Rs 72 crore of its Rs 100 crore in government securities. Consider the following statements. items.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: 72 out of 100 is 72 percent. Statement 2 is incorrect: 72 is less than 80. Statement 3 is correct: 80 minus 72 is 8.

items.question: The 2023 Cricket World Cup final was played at Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad, where Australia beat India. India won the 2024 T20 World Cup final against South Africa in Barbados. A quiz awards 1 mark for each correct statement and deducts 1 mark for each incorrect statement. A student marks these statements: (1) India won both finals. (2) Both finals were played in India.
